explanation: Marker A identifies the Deltoid tuberosity. The deltoid tuberosity is a rough lateral shaft prominence that receives the deltoid insertion.

distractorExplanations.B: Acromion is not the marked target. The acromion continues laterally from the scapular spine and forms the bony roof above the shoulder joint.
distractorExplanations.C: Clavicle is not the marked target. An S-shaped subcutaneous strut between the manubrium and acromion that holds the upper limb away from the trunk and transmits load to the axial skeleton.
distractorExplanations.D: Coracoid process is not the marked target. A hook-shaped projection from the superior scapula, lying anterior to the glenoid and serving as an attachment for muscles and ligaments.

learningObjective: Identify the Deltoid tuberosity and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the C5 root of brachial plexus. The C5 ventral ramus emerges between the anterior and middle scalene muscles and joins C6 to form the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

distractorExplanations.B: C7 root of brachial plexus is not the marked target. The C7 ventral ramus continues by itself as the middle trunk before dividing behind the clavicle.
distractorExplanations.C: C6 root of brachial plexus is not the marked target. The C6 ventral ramus passes through the interscalene interval and joins C5 to complete the upper trunk.
distractorExplanations.D: C8 root of brachial plexus is not the marked target. The C8 ventral ramus ascends over the first rib to join T1 and form the lower trunk of the brachial plexus.

learningObjective: Identify the C5 root of brachial plexus and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

media.attribution: Source: Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. Educational reference from the local study library.

annotations.label: C5 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C5 ventral ramus emerges between the anterior and middle scalene muscles and joins C6 to form the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

annotations.label: C6 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C6 ventral ramus passes through the interscalene interval and joins C5 to complete the upper trunk.

annotations.label: C7 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C7 ventral ramus continues by itself as the middle trunk before dividing behind the clavicle.

annotations.label: C8 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C8 ventral ramus ascends over the first rib to join T1 and form the lower trunk of the brachial plexus.

annotations.label: T1 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: Most of the T1 ventral ramus joins C8 above the first rib to form the lower trunk; a smaller part remains as the first intercostal nerve.

annotations.label: Dorsal scapular nerve
annotations.description: A branch usually arising from the C5 root that pierces middle scalene and descends along the medial border of the scapula with the dorsal scapular artery.

annotations.label: Upper trunk of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The union of the C5 and C6 ventral rami at the lateral border of the scalene interval, dividing into anterior and posterior divisions above the clavicle.

annotations.label: Middle trunk of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The continuation of the C7 ventral ramus through the interscalene interval, dividing into anterior and posterior divisions behind the clavicle.

annotations.label: Lower trunk of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The union of C8 and T1 ventral rami, lying inferiorly in the plexus before dividing behind the clavicle.

annotations.label: Medial cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord medial to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior division of the lower trunk.

annotations.label: Lateral cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord lateral to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior divisions of the upper and middle trunks.

annotations.label: Posterior cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord posterior to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by all three posterior divisions.

annotations.label: Suprascapular nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the upper trunk that crosses the posterior triangle and passes under the superior transverse scapular ligament into the supraspinous fossa.

annotations.label: Lateral pectoral nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the lateral cord that crosses anterior to the axillary artery, pierces clavipectoral fascia and chiefly supplies pectoralis major.

annotations.label: Medial pectoral nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the medial cord that typically pierces pectoralis minor and continues into the deep surface of pectoralis major.

annotations.label: Axillary artery
annotations.description: The continuation of the subclavian from the lateral border of the first rib to the inferior border of teres major, where it becomes brachial.

annotations.label: Musculocutaneous nerve
annotations.description: A C5–C7 terminal branch of the lateral cord that pierces coracobrachialis and descends between biceps and brachialis before continuing as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm.

annotations.label: Axillary nerve
annotations.description: A C5–C6 terminal branch of the posterior cord that passes through the quadrangular space with the posterior circumflex humeral artery and winds around the surgical neck.

annotations.label: Median nerve
annotations.description: A terminal nerve formed by lateral and medial roots around the axillary artery, descending with the brachial artery and entering the hand through the carpal tunnel.

annotations.label: Radial nerve
annotations.description: A large terminal branch of the posterior cord that passes through the triangular interval, winds in the radial groove and divides near the lateral elbow into superficial sensory and deep motor branches.

annotations.label: Ulnar nerve
annotations.description: A C8–T1 dominant terminal branch of the medial cord that passes behind the medial epicondyle, between the heads of flexor carpi ulnaris and into the hand superficial to the flexor retinaculum in Guyon's canal.

annotations.label: Thoracodorsal nerve
annotations.description: A posterior-cord branch that descends along the posterior axillary wall with the thoracodorsal vessels to reach latissimus dorsi.

annotations.label: Medial cutaneous nerve of arm
annotations.description: A small medial-cord branch that descends along the medial axillary and brachial vessels to supply skin of the medial arm.

annotations.label: Medial cutaneous nerve of forearm
annotations.description: A medial-cord sensory branch that descends with the basilic vein, pierces deep fascia in the arm and divides into anterior and posterior branches for the medial forearm.

annotations.label: Long thoracic nerve
annotations.description: The long thoracic nerve arises from C5-C7 roots and descends superficially on serratus anterior along the lateral thoracic wall.

explanation: Marker A identifies the Long thoracic nerve. The long thoracic nerve arises from C5-C7 roots and descends superficially on serratus anterior along the lateral thoracic wall.

distractorExplanations.A: C5 root of brachial plexus is not the marked target. The C5 ventral ramus emerges between the anterior and middle scalene muscles and joins C6 to form the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.
distractorExplanations.C: C7 root of brachial plexus is not the marked target. The C7 ventral ramus continues by itself as the middle trunk before dividing behind the clavicle.
distractorExplanations.D: C6 root of brachial plexus is not the marked target. The C6 ventral ramus passes through the interscalene interval and joins C5 to complete the upper trunk.

learningObjective: Identify the Long thoracic nerve and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: C5 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C5 ventral ramus emerges between the anterior and middle scalene muscles and joins C6 to form the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

annotations.label: C6 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C6 ventral ramus passes through the interscalene interval and joins C5 to complete the upper trunk.

annotations.label: C7 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C7 ventral ramus continues by itself as the middle trunk before dividing behind the clavicle.

annotations.label: C8 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C8 ventral ramus ascends over the first rib to join T1 and form the lower trunk of the brachial plexus.

annotations.label: T1 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: Most of the T1 ventral ramus joins C8 above the first rib to form the lower trunk; a smaller part remains as the first intercostal nerve.

annotations.label: Dorsal scapular nerve
annotations.description: A branch usually arising from the C5 root that pierces middle scalene and descends along the medial border of the scapula with the dorsal scapular artery.

annotations.label: Upper trunk of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The union of the C5 and C6 ventral rami at the lateral border of the scalene interval, dividing into anterior and posterior divisions above the clavicle.

annotations.label: Middle trunk of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The continuation of the C7 ventral ramus through the interscalene interval, dividing into anterior and posterior divisions behind the clavicle.

annotations.label: Lower trunk of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The union of C8 and T1 ventral rami, lying inferiorly in the plexus before dividing behind the clavicle.

annotations.label: Medial cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord medial to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior division of the lower trunk.

annotations.label: Lateral cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord lateral to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior divisions of the upper and middle trunks.

annotations.label: Posterior cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord posterior to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by all three posterior divisions.

annotations.label: Suprascapular nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the upper trunk that crosses the posterior triangle and passes under the superior transverse scapular ligament into the supraspinous fossa.

annotations.label: Lateral pectoral nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the lateral cord that crosses anterior to the axillary artery, pierces clavipectoral fascia and chiefly supplies pectoralis major.

annotations.label: Medial pectoral nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the medial cord that typically pierces pectoralis minor and continues into the deep surface of pectoralis major.

annotations.label: Axillary artery
annotations.description: The continuation of the subclavian from the lateral border of the first rib to the inferior border of teres major, where it becomes brachial.

annotations.label: Musculocutaneous nerve
annotations.description: A C5–C7 terminal branch of the lateral cord that pierces coracobrachialis and descends between biceps and brachialis before continuing as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm.

annotations.label: Axillary nerve
annotations.description: A C5–C6 terminal branch of the posterior cord that passes through the quadrangular space with the posterior circumflex humeral artery and winds around the surgical neck.

annotations.label: Median nerve
annotations.description: A terminal nerve formed by lateral and medial roots around the axillary artery, descending with the brachial artery and entering the hand through the carpal tunnel.

annotations.label: Radial nerve
annotations.description: A large terminal branch of the posterior cord that passes through the triangular interval, winds in the radial groove and divides near the lateral elbow into superficial sensory and deep motor branches.

annotations.label: Ulnar nerve
annotations.description: A C8–T1 dominant terminal branch of the medial cord that passes behind the medial epicondyle, between the heads of flexor carpi ulnaris and into the hand superficial to the flexor retinaculum in Guyon's canal.

annotations.label: Thoracodorsal nerve
annotations.description: A posterior-cord branch that descends along the posterior axillary wall with the thoracodorsal vessels to reach latissimus dorsi.

annotations.label: Medial cutaneous nerve of arm
annotations.description: A small medial-cord branch that descends along the medial axillary and brachial vessels to supply skin of the medial arm.

annotations.label: Medial cutaneous nerve of forearm
annotations.description: A medial-cord sensory branch that descends with the basilic vein, pierces deep fascia in the arm and divides into anterior and posterior branches for the medial forearm.

annotations.label: Long thoracic nerve
annotations.description: The long thoracic nerve arises from C5-C7 roots and descends superficially on serratus anterior along the lateral thoracic wall.

subject: anatomy
topic: Deep muscles of the shoulder girdle
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Deltoid. A thick multipennate muscle forming the rounded shoulder, arising from the lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and inserting on the deltoid tuberosity.

distractorExplanations.B: Serratus anterior is not the marked target. Serratus anterior attaches the lateral thoracic wall to the anterior surface of the medial scapular border.
distractorExplanations.C: Pectoralis major is not the marked target. Pectoralis major converges from the clavicle and anterior chest wall to the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus.
distractorExplanations.D: Coracobrachialis is not the marked target. Coracobrachialis runs from the coracoid process to the medial humeral shaft and is pierced by the musculocutaneous nerve.

learningObjective: Identify the Deltoid and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

source.title: Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice

media.alt: Gray's Anatomy 42nd edition, Figure 49.28: Deep muscles of the shoulder girdle, anterior and posterior view, with original leader lines and labels.
media.caption: Deep muscles of the shoulder girdle
media.attribution: Source: Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. Educational reference from the local study library.

annotations.label: Deltoid
annotations.description: A thick multipennate muscle forming the rounded shoulder, arising from the lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and inserting on the deltoid tuberosity.

annotations.label: Coracobrachialis
annotations.description: Coracobrachialis runs from the coracoid process to the medial humeral shaft and is pierced by the musculocutaneous nerve.

annotations.label: Pectoralis major
annotations.description: Pectoralis major converges from the clavicle and anterior chest wall to the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus.

annotations.label: Serratus anterior
annotations.description: Serratus anterior attaches the lateral thoracic wall to the anterior surface of the medial scapular border.

annotations.label: Supraspinatus
annotations.description: A rotator-cuff muscle arising in the supraspinous fossa, passing beneath the acromion and inserting on the superior facet of the greater tubercle.

annotations.label: Subscapularis
annotations.description: A broad rotator-cuff muscle filling the subscapular fossa on the anterior scapula and inserting on the lesser tubercle of the humerus.

annotations.label: Teres major
annotations.description: Teres major passes from the inferior scapula to the medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus and contributes to the posterior axillary fold.

annotations.label: Coraco-acromial ligament
annotations.description: A strong triangular band from the coracoid process to the acromion that forms the roof of the coracoacromial arch above the humeral head.

annotations.label: Pectoralis minor
annotations.description: Pectoralis minor passes from the upper ribs to the coracoid process and forms part of the anterior wall of the axilla.

annotations.label: Subclavius
annotations.description: Subclavius lies below the clavicle and runs from the first rib and its costal cartilage to the inferior clavicular surface.

annotations.label: Clavicle
annotations.description: An S-shaped subcutaneous strut between the manubrium and acromion that holds the upper limb away from the trunk and transmits load to the axial skeleton.

annotations.label: Levator scapulae
annotations.description: Levator scapulae descends from upper cervical transverse processes to the upper medial border of the scapula.

annotations.label: Infraspinatus
annotations.description: A broad rotator-cuff muscle occupying the infraspinous fossa and inserting on the middle facet of the greater tubercle.

annotations.label: Teres minor
annotations.description: A narrow rotator-cuff muscle along the lateral scapular border that inserts on the inferior facet of the greater tubercle.

annotations.label: Latissimus dorsi
annotations.description: Latissimus dorsi passes from the back to the floor of the humeral intertubercular sulcus and forms part of the posterior axillary fold.

annotations.label: Trapezius
annotations.description: Trapezius attaches to the lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and helps position and rotate the scapula.

prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Medial cutaneous nerve of forearm. A medial-cord sensory branch that descends with the basilic vein, pierces deep fascia in the arm and divides into anterior and posterior branches for the medial forearm.

distractorExplanations.A: Suprascapular nerve is not the marked target. A branch of the upper trunk that crosses the posterior triangle and passes under the superior transverse scapular ligament into the supraspinous fossa.
distractorExplanations.B: Deltoid is not the marked target. A thick multipennate muscle forming the rounded shoulder, arising from the lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and inserting on the deltoid tuberosity.
distractorExplanations.D: Brachial vein is not the marked target. The deep brachial veins accompany the brachial artery in the arm and contribute to the axillary venous drainage.

learningObjective: Identify the Medial cutaneous nerve of forearm and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Medial cutaneous nerve of forearm
annotations.description: A medial-cord sensory branch that descends with the basilic vein, pierces deep fascia in the arm and divides into anterior and posterior branches for the medial forearm.

annotations.label: Suprascapular nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the upper trunk that crosses the posterior triangle and passes under the superior transverse scapular ligament into the supraspinous fossa.

annotations.label: Brachial vein
annotations.description: The deep brachial veins accompany the brachial artery in the arm and contribute to the axillary venous drainage.

annotations.label: Deltoid
annotations.description: A thick multipennate muscle forming the rounded shoulder, arising from the lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and inserting on the deltoid tuberosity.

annotations.label: Pectoralis minor
annotations.description: Pectoralis minor passes from the upper ribs to the coracoid process and forms part of the anterior wall of the axilla.

annotations.label: Lateral cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord lateral to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior divisions of the upper and middle trunks.

annotations.label: Axillary artery
annotations.description: The continuation of the subclavian from the lateral border of the first rib to the inferior border of teres major, where it becomes brachial.

annotations.label: Coracobrachialis
annotations.description: Coracobrachialis runs from the coracoid process to the medial humeral shaft and is pierced by the musculocutaneous nerve.

annotations.label: Musculocutaneous nerve
annotations.description: A C5–C7 terminal branch of the lateral cord that pierces coracobrachialis and descends between biceps and brachialis before continuing as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm.

annotations.label: Biceps brachii, short and long heads
annotations.description: A two-headed anterior arm muscle whose long head arises from the supraglenoid tubercle and short head from the coracoid, joining to insert on the radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis.

annotations.label: Median nerve
annotations.description: A terminal nerve formed by lateral and medial roots around the axillary artery, descending with the brachial artery and entering the hand through the carpal tunnel.

annotations.label: Brachial artery
annotations.description: The continuation of the axillary artery below teres major, running with the median nerve in the medial bicipital groove and dividing into radial and ulnar arteries in the cubital fossa.

annotations.label: Medial cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord medial to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior division of the lower trunk.

annotations.label: Posterior cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord posterior to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by all three posterior divisions.

annotations.label: Subscapularis
annotations.description: A broad rotator-cuff muscle filling the subscapular fossa on the anterior scapula and inserting on the lesser tubercle of the humerus.

annotations.label: Thoracodorsal nerve
annotations.description: A posterior-cord branch that descends along the posterior axillary wall with the thoracodorsal vessels to reach latissimus dorsi.

annotations.label: Medial cutaneous nerve of arm
annotations.description: A small medial-cord branch that descends along the medial axillary and brachial vessels to supply skin of the medial arm.

annotations.label: Radial nerve
annotations.description: A large terminal branch of the posterior cord that passes through the triangular interval, winds in the radial groove and divides near the lateral elbow into superficial sensory and deep motor branches.

annotations.label: Profunda brachii artery
annotations.description: The profunda brachii artery accompanies the radial nerve through the posterior arm and supplies the triceps region.

annotations.label: Ulnar nerve
annotations.description: A C8–T1 dominant terminal branch of the medial cord that passes behind the medial epicondyle, between the heads of flexor carpi ulnaris and into the hand superficial to the flexor retinaculum in Guyon's canal.

annotations.label: Basilic vein
annotations.description: A superficial vein ascending medially from the hand and forearm, piercing deep fascia in the mid-arm and joining brachial veins to form the axillary vein near teres major.

annotations.label: Cephalic vein
annotations.description: A superficial vein ascending on the lateral forearm and arm, then running in the deltopectoral groove to pierce clavipectoral fascia and drain into the axillary vein.

annotations.label: Biceps brachii
annotations.description: A two-headed anterior arm muscle whose long head arises from the supraglenoid tubercle and short head from the coracoid, joining to insert on the radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis.

annotations.label: Brachialis
annotations.description: A deep anterior arm muscle from the distal anterior humerus to the ulnar tuberosity and coronoid process.

annotations.label: Median nerve
annotations.description: A terminal nerve formed by lateral and medial roots around the axillary artery, descending with the brachial artery and entering the hand through the carpal tunnel.

annotations.label: Brachial artery
annotations.description: The continuation of the axillary artery below teres major, running with the median nerve in the medial bicipital groove and dividing into radial and ulnar arteries in the cubital fossa.

annotations.label: Brachioradialis
annotations.description: A superficial posterolateral forearm muscle running from the lateral supracondylar ridge to the distal radius near the styloid process.

annotations.label: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
annotations.description: A superficial posterior forearm muscle from the common extensor origin to the base of the third metacarpal.

annotations.label: Flexor digitorum superficialis
annotations.description: An intermediate anterior forearm muscle that divides into four tendons, each splitting around a profundus tendon to insert on the sides of a middle phalanx.

annotations.label: Flexor pollicis longus
annotations.description: A deep anterior forearm muscle whose tendon traverses the carpal tunnel to the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb.

annotations.label: Flexor carpi radialis
annotations.description: A superficial anterior forearm muscle from the medial epicondyle to the bases of the second and third metacarpals on the radial side.

annotations.label: Abductor pollicis longus
annotations.description: A deep posterior forearm muscle whose tendon crosses the radial wrist to the base of the first metacarpal.

annotations.label: Radial artery
annotations.description: A terminal branch of the brachial artery that descends along the lateral forearm, crosses the anatomical snuffbox and enters the palm to form most of the deep palmar arch.

annotations.label: Pronator quadratus
annotations.description: A flat, deep distal-forearm muscle spanning the anterior ulna to the anterior radius immediately proximal to the wrist.

annotations.label: Extensor pollicis brevis
annotations.description: A deep posterior forearm muscle whose tendon runs with abductor pollicis longus to the base of the proximal thumb phalanx.

annotations.label: Supinator
annotations.description: A deep proximal posterior forearm muscle wrapping around the upper radius from the lateral epicondyle, annular ligament and supinator crest of the ulna.

annotations.label: Pronator teres
annotations.description: A superficial proximal forearm muscle with humeral and ulnar heads that crosses to the lateral midshaft of the radius.

annotations.label: Ulnar artery
annotations.description: The larger terminal branch of the brachial artery, passing deep to pronator teres and then with the ulnar nerve toward the palm, where it forms most of the superficial palmar arch.

annotations.label: Flexor carpi ulnaris
annotations.description: A superficial anterior forearm muscle with humeral and ulnar heads, inserting through the pisiform onto the hamate and fifth metacarpal.

annotations.label: Palmaris longus
annotations.description: A slender superficial anterior forearm muscle whose long tendon passes superficial to the flexor retinaculum into the palmar aponeurosis.

annotations.label: Ulnar nerve, dorsal branch
annotations.description: A sensory branch arising in the distal forearm that winds posteriorly beneath flexor carpi ulnaris to reach the dorsomedial hand.

annotations.label: Ulnar nerve
annotations.description: A C8–T1 dominant terminal branch of the medial cord that passes behind the medial epicondyle, between the heads of flexor carpi ulnaris and into the hand superficial to the flexor retinaculum in Guyon's canal.

annotations.label: Radius

annotations.label: Abductor digiti minimi

subject: anatomy
topic: Deep palmar arch and its branches
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Common palmar digital artery. Common palmar digital arteries arise from the superficial palmar arch and divide into proper digital branches toward adjacent fingers.

distractorExplanations.A: Ulnar artery is not the marked target. The larger terminal branch of the brachial artery, passing deep to pronator teres and then with the ulnar nerve toward the palm, where it forms most of the superficial palmar arch.
distractorExplanations.B: Superficial palmar arch is not the marked target. An arterial arcade lying just deep to the palmar aponeurosis, formed mainly by the ulnar artery and usually completed by a superficial radial contribution.
distractorExplanations.D: Guyon's canal is not the marked target. Guyon's canal carries the ulnar nerve and artery into the palm on the ulnar side of the wrist, superficial to the flexor retinaculum.

learningObjective: Identify the Common palmar digital artery and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Ilium
annotations.description: The ilium is the broad superior part of the hip bone, expanding above the acetabulum into the iliac wing.

annotations.label: Pubis
annotations.description: The pubis is the anteroinferior part of the hip bone and contributes to the acetabulum and obturator foramen.

annotations.label: Ischium
annotations.description: The ischium forms the posteroinferior part of the hip bone and bears the ischial tuberosity.

annotations.label: Femur
annotations.description: The femur is the long bone of the thigh, extending from the hip to the knee with a head, neck, trochanters, shaft, condyles, and epicondyles.

annotations.label: Patella
annotations.description: The patella is a sesamoid bone embedded in the quadriceps tendon anterior to the knee, with its apex continuing into the patellar ligament.

annotations.label: Tibia
annotations.description: The tibia is the large medial weight-bearing bone of the leg, articulating with the femur, fibula, and talus. Its proximal condyles form the tibial plateau and its distal projection is the medial malleolus.

annotations.label: Fibula
annotations.description: The fibula is the slender lateral bone of the leg, joined to the tibia proximally and distally; its distal end forms the lateral malleolus.

annotations.label: Talus
annotations.description: The talus receives the tibia and fibula at the ankle and transmits load to the calcaneus and navicular.

annotations.label: Navicular
annotations.description: The navicular lies between the talar head and the three cuneiforms on the medial side of the foot.

annotations.label: Medial cuneiform
annotations.description: The medial cuneiform lies between the navicular and the base of the first metatarsal.

annotations.label: Calcaneus
annotations.description: The calcaneus forms the heel, lies below the talus and articulates anteriorly with the cuboid.

annotations.label: Metatarsals
annotations.description: The metatarsals form the long bones between the tarsus and the proximal toe phalanges.

annotations.label: Phalanges
annotations.description: Four lateral toes each have proximal, middle, and distal phalanges, whereas the great toe has only proximal and distal phalanges.

prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Femoral nerve. The femoral nerve arises from posterior divisions of L2-L4, emerges lateral to psoas major, and passes deep to the inguinal ligament into the femoral triangle.

distractorExplanations.A: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve is not the marked target. A purely sensory lumbar-plexus branch that crosses iliacus toward the ASIS and passes under or through the inguinal ligament to the anterolateral thigh.
distractorExplanations.B: Inguinal ligament is not the marked target. The inguinal ligament spans the anterior superior iliac spine and pubic tubercle, forming the superior boundary of the femoral triangle.
distractorExplanations.C: Iliopsoas is not the marked target. Iliacus and psoas major unite deep to the inguinal ligament and insert on the lesser trochanter.

learningObjective: Identify the Femoral nerve and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
topic: Gluteal region and posterior thigh neurovascular anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Medial femoral circumflex artery. The medial circumflex femoral artery passes toward the posterior proximal femur and contributes the principal retinacular supply to the adult femoral head.

distractorExplanations.A: Gluteus medius is not the marked target. Gluteus medius lies deep to gluteus maximus on the lateral ilium and inserts on the greater trochanter.
distractorExplanations.C: Common fibular nerve is not the marked target. This terminal branch of the sciatic nerve follows the biceps femoris tendon and winds around the fibular neck before dividing into superficial and deep fibular nerves.
distractorExplanations.D: Small saphenous vein is not the marked target. The small saphenous vein begins laterally in the dorsal venous arch, passes posterior to the lateral malleolus, and ascends the posterior calf to drain into the popliteal vein.

learningObjective: Identify the Medial femoral circumflex artery and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
topic: Cruciate ligaments and menisci of the knee
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Intercondylar region. The intercondylar region lies between the femoral condyles and accommodates the cruciate ligaments.

distractorExplanations.A: Medial meniscus is not the marked target. The C-shaped medial meniscus lies on the medial tibial plateau and is firmly attached to the capsule and tibial collateral ligament.
distractorExplanations.C: Lateral meniscus is not the marked target. The nearly circular lateral meniscus lies on the lateral tibial plateau and is separated from the fibular collateral ligament by the popliteus tendon.
distractorExplanations.D: Posterior cruciate ligament is not the marked target. The PCL runs from the posterior intercondylar area of the tibia upward, forward, and medially to the lateral surface of the medial femoral condyle.

learningObjective: Identify the Intercondylar region and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Patella. The patella is a sesamoid bone embedded in the quadriceps tendon anterior to the knee, with its apex continuing into the patellar ligament.

distractorExplanations.A: Fibularis longus is not the marked target. Fibularis longus occupies the lateral leg, then passes behind the lateral malleolus and beneath the foot toward the first metatarsal and medial cuneiform.
distractorExplanations.C: Iliotibial tract is not the marked target. The iliotibial tract is a thickened lateral portion of fascia lata that receives tensor fasciae latae and gluteus maximus.
distractorExplanations.D: Patellar ligament is not the marked target. The patellar ligament connects the apex of the patella to the tibial tuberosity as the distal continuation of the knee extensor mechanism.

learningObjective: Identify the Patella and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Patella
annotations.description: The patella is a sesamoid bone embedded in the quadriceps tendon anterior to the knee, with its apex continuing into the patellar ligament.

annotations.label: Iliotibial tract
annotations.description: The iliotibial tract is a thickened lateral portion of fascia lata that receives tensor fasciae latae and gluteus maximus.

annotations.label: Patellar ligament
annotations.description: The patellar ligament connects the apex of the patella to the tibial tuberosity as the distal continuation of the knee extensor mechanism.

annotations.label: Fibularis longus
annotations.description: Fibularis longus occupies the lateral leg, then passes behind the lateral malleolus and beneath the foot toward the first metatarsal and medial cuneiform.

annotations.label: Tibialis anterior
annotations.description: This superficial anterior-compartment muscle runs from the lateral tibia to the medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal.

annotations.label: Extensor digitorum longus
annotations.description: This anterior-compartment muscle descends to four tendons for the lateral four toes.

annotations.label: Fibularis brevis
annotations.description: Fibularis brevis lies deep to fibularis longus and inserts on the tuberosity at the base of the fifth metatarsal.

annotations.label: Extensor hallucis longus
annotations.description: A deep anterior-leg muscle between tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus whose tendon reaches the distal hallux phalanx.

annotations.label: Lateral malleolus
annotations.description: The lateral malleolus is the distal fibular prominence on the lateral side of the ankle.

annotations.label: Extensor digitorum brevis
annotations.description: Extensor digitorum brevis lies on the dorsum of the foot and extends toes two through four.

annotations.label: Tibial tuberosity
annotations.description: The tibial tuberosity is the anterior proximal tibial prominence receiving the patellar ligament.

annotations.label: Gastrocnemius
annotations.description: The two-headed gastrocnemius arises above the femoral condyles and joins soleus in the calcaneal tendon.

annotations.label: Soleus
annotations.description: Soleus is the broad postural muscle deep to gastrocnemius, arising from the tibia and fibula and joining the calcaneal tendon.

annotations.label: Tibia
annotations.description: The tibia is the large medial weight-bearing bone of the leg, articulating with the femur, fibula, and talus. Its proximal condyles form the tibial plateau and its distal projection is the medial malleolus.

annotations.label: Medial malleolus
annotations.description: The medial malleolus is the distal tibial projection on the medial side of the ankle.

annotations.label: Extensor hallucis brevis
annotations.description: Extensor hallucis brevis is the medial short extensor on the dorsum of the foot and inserts into the hallux proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Fibularis tertius
annotations.description: A variable anterior-compartment muscle, often continuous with extensor digitorum longus, inserting on the dorsal base of the fifth metatarsal.

annotations.label: Biceps femoris
annotations.description: The long and short heads form the lateral hamstring and insert mainly on the head of the fibula.

annotations.label: Head of fibula
annotations.description: The fibular head is the expanded proximal fibula and articulates with the lateral tibial condyle.

annotations.label: Calcaneal tendon
annotations.description: The calcaneal tendon combines the gastrocnemius and soleus tendons and inserts into the posterior calcaneus.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Metatarsals. Five metatarsals form the forefoot between the tarsals and proximal phalanges, each with a base, shaft, and head.

distractorExplanations.B: Phalanges is not the marked target. Four lateral toes each have proximal, middle, and distal phalanges, whereas the great toe has only proximal and distal phalanges.
distractorExplanations.C: Calcaneus is not the marked target. The calcaneus forms the heel, lies below the talus and articulates anteriorly with the cuboid.
distractorExplanations.D: Talus is not the marked target. The talus receives the tibia and fibula at the ankle and transmits load to the calcaneus and navicular.

learningObjective: Identify the Metatarsals and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
topic: Plantar nerves and vessels between muscle layers
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Common plantar digital nerves. The common plantar digital nerves run forward in the sole and divide into proper digital branches for adjacent toes.

distractorExplanations.B: Abductor digiti minimi is not the marked target. In the foot, abductor digiti minimi occupies the lateral sole and inserts on the lateral side of the fifth toe proximal phalanx.
distractorExplanations.C: Lateral plantar artery is not the marked target. The larger terminal branch of the posterior tibial artery that crosses the lateral sole and turns medially to form most of the deep plantar arch.
distractorExplanations.D: Plantar aponeurosis is not the marked target. The plantar aponeurosis runs from the calcaneal tuberosity toward the toes and supports the longitudinal arch.

learningObjective: Identify the Common plantar digital nerves and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

source.title: Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice

annotations.label: Common plantar digital nerves
annotations.description: The common plantar digital nerves run forward in the sole and divide into proper digital branches for adjacent toes.

annotations.label: Lateral plantar artery
annotations.description: The larger terminal branch of the posterior tibial artery that crosses the lateral sole and turns medially to form most of the deep plantar arch.

annotations.label: Abductor digiti minimi
annotations.description: In the foot, abductor digiti minimi occupies the lateral sole and inserts on the lateral side of the fifth toe proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Plantar aponeurosis
annotations.description: The plantar aponeurosis runs from the calcaneal tuberosity toward the toes and supports the longitudinal arch.

annotations.label: Lateral plantar nerve
annotations.description: The smaller tibial terminal branch runs obliquely across the sole with the lateral plantar artery and divides into superficial and deep branches.

annotations.label: Posterior tibial artery
annotations.description: This terminal branch of the popliteal artery descends in the deep posterior compartment and passes behind the medial malleolus into the sole.

annotations.label: Flexor retinaculum
annotations.description: The ankle flexor retinaculum extends from the medial malleolus to the calcaneus and roofs the tarsal tunnel.

annotations.label: Medial plantar nerve
annotations.description: The larger tibial terminal branch runs forward in the sole with the medial plantar artery between abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis.

annotations.label: Flexor accessorius
annotations.description: Flexor accessorius, also called quadratus plantae, arises from the calcaneus and joins the flexor digitorum longus tendons.

annotations.label: Abductor hallucis
annotations.description: Abductor hallucis occupies the medial margin of the sole and inserts on the medial side of the hallux proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Flexor hallucis brevis
annotations.description: Flexor hallucis brevis is a short plantar muscle whose two heads insert on either side of the base of the hallux proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Flexor digitorum brevis
annotations.description: Flexor digitorum brevis lies in the first plantar muscle layer and sends divided tendons to the middle phalanges of toes two through five.

distractorExplanations.A: Abductor digiti minimi is not the marked target. In the foot, abductor digiti minimi occupies the lateral sole and inserts on the lateral side of the fifth toe proximal phalanx.

distractorExplanations.D: Plantar aponeurosis is not the marked target. The plantar aponeurosis runs from the calcaneal tuberosity toward the toes and supports the longitudinal arch.

learningObjective: Identify the Flexor hallucis brevis and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
chapter: 39 - Nose, nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Nasal bone. The nasal bone forms the bony bridge above the lateral nasal cartilage.

distractorExplanations.A: Vomer is not the marked target. The vomer forms the posteroinferior part of the bony nasal septum.
distractorExplanations.B: Septal cartilage is not the marked target. The septal cartilage forms the anterior cartilaginous part of the nasal septum.
distractorExplanations.D: Lateral nasal cartilage is not the marked target. The lateral nasal cartilage lies below the nasal bone in the external nasal skeleton.

learningObjective: Identify the Nasal bone and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

options.text: Orifice of posterior ethmoidal air cells

acceptedFreeText: Orifice of posterior ethmoidal air cells
explanation: Marker A identifies the Orifice of posterior ethmoidal air cells. The posterior ethmoidal air cells open into the superior meatus.

distractorExplanations.B: Orifices of bullar sinuses is not the marked target. The bullar ethmoidal openings lie at the ethmoidal bulla in the middle meatus.
distractorExplanations.C: Hiatus semilunaris is not the marked target. The hiatus semilunaris is the curved cleft below the ethmoidal bulla in the middle meatus.
distractorExplanations.D: Orifice of maxillary sinus is not the marked target. The maxillary sinus opens high on its medial wall into the middle meatus.

learningObjective: Identify the Orifice of posterior ethmoidal air cells and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Anterior ethmoidal artery. The anterior ethmoidal artery supplies the anterosuperior nasal cavity.

distractorExplanations.A: Middle nasal concha is not the marked target. The middle concha is the intermediate projection on the lateral nasal wall.
distractorExplanations.C: Posterior ethmoidal artery is not the marked target. The posterior ethmoidal artery contributes to the blood supply of the posterosuperior nasal cavity.
distractorExplanations.D: Superior nasal concha is not the marked target. The superior concha is shown on the lateral wall beneath the posterior ethmoidal artery.

learningObjective: Identify the Anterior ethmoidal artery and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Anterior ethmoidal artery
annotations.description: The anterior ethmoidal artery supplies the anterosuperior nasal cavity.

annotations.label: Posterior ethmoidal artery
annotations.description: The posterior ethmoidal artery contributes to the blood supply of the posterosuperior nasal cavity.

annotations.label: Superior nasal concha
annotations.description: The superior concha is shown on the lateral wall beneath the posterior ethmoidal artery.

annotations.label: Middle nasal concha
annotations.description: The middle concha is the intermediate projection on the lateral nasal wall.

annotations.label: Inferior nasal concha
annotations.description: The inferior concha forms the lowest turbinate on the lateral nasal wall.

annotations.label: Lateral branches of sphenopalatine artery
annotations.description: These branches distribute over the lateral wall after the sphenopalatine artery enters the nasal cavity.

annotations.label: Septal branch of sphenopalatine artery
annotations.description: This branch crosses to the septum and runs forward over its surface.

annotations.label: Terminal part of greater palatine artery
annotations.description: The greater palatine artery reaches the anterior nasal septum through the incisive canal.

prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Anterior ethmoidal artery. The anterior ethmoidal artery supplies the anterosuperior nasal cavity.

distractorExplanations.B: Posterior ethmoidal artery is not the marked target. The posterior ethmoidal artery contributes to the blood supply of the posterosuperior nasal cavity.
distractorExplanations.C: Middle nasal concha is not the marked target. The middle concha is the intermediate projection on the lateral nasal wall.
distractorExplanations.D: Inferior nasal concha is not the marked target. The inferior concha forms the lowest turbinate on the lateral nasal wall.

learningObjective: Identify the Anterior ethmoidal artery and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

explanation: Marker A identifies the Epiglottis. The epiglottis is the leaf-shaped cartilage projecting superiorly behind the hyoid.

distractorExplanations.A: Corniculate cartilage is not the marked target. The corniculate cartilage sits on the apex of the arytenoid cartilage.
distractorExplanations.C: Thyrohyoid membrane is not the marked target. The thyrohyoid membrane spans between the hyoid bone and thyroid cartilage.
distractorExplanations.D: Arytenoid cartilage is not the marked target. Each arytenoid cartilage rests on the superior border of the cricoid lamina.

learningObjective: Identify the Epiglottis and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

explanation: Marker A identifies the Corniculate cartilage. The corniculate cartilage is a small nodule above the arytenoid apex.

distractorExplanations.A: Cricoid cartilage is not the marked target. The cricoid cartilage lies inferior to the thyroid cartilage and supports the lower larynx.
distractorExplanations.C: Epiglottis is not the marked target. The epiglottis forms the anterior attachment region of the quadrangular membrane.
distractorExplanations.D: Conus elasticus is not the marked target. The conus elasticus extends upward from the cricoid cartilage to the vocal ligament.

learningObjective: Identify the Corniculate cartilage and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

learningObjective: Identify the Epiglottis and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle. Posterior cricoarytenoid abducts the vocal folds by rotating the arytenoid cartilages.

distractorExplanations.A: Oblique arytenoid muscle is not the marked target. The oblique arytenoid muscles cross between the arytenoids and help narrow the laryngeal inlet.
distractorExplanations.B: Transverse arytenoid muscle is not the marked target. The transverse interarytenoid muscle draws the arytenoid cartilages together.
distractorExplanations.C: Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle is not the marked target. Lateral cricoarytenoid rotates the arytenoid to adduct the vocal fold.

learningObjective: Identify the Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle
annotations.description: Posterior cricoarytenoid abducts the vocal folds by rotating the arytenoid cartilages.

annotations.label: Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle
annotations.description: Lateral cricoarytenoid rotates the arytenoid to adduct the vocal fold.

annotations.label: Transverse arytenoid muscle
annotations.description: The transverse interarytenoid muscle draws the arytenoid cartilages together.

annotations.label: Oblique arytenoid muscle
annotations.description: The oblique arytenoid muscles cross between the arytenoids and help narrow the laryngeal inlet.

annotations.label: Thyroarytenoid muscle
annotations.description: Thyroarytenoid shortens the vocal fold by drawing the arytenoid toward the thyroid cartilage.

annotations.label: Vocalis muscle
annotations.description: Vocalis lies alongside the vocal ligament and adjusts its local tension.

annotations.label: Cricothyroid muscle
annotations.description: Cricothyroid tilts the thyroid relative to the cricoid and increases vocal fold tension.

annotations.label: Vocal ligament
annotations.description: The vocal ligament extends from the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid vocal process.

annotations.label: Thyroid cartilage
annotations.description: The thyroid cartilage provides the anterior attachment for the vocal ligament and intrinsic muscles.

annotations.label: Cricoid cartilage
annotations.description: The cricoid supports the arytenoids and gives origin to the cricoarytenoid muscles.

annotations.label: Arytenoid cartilage
annotations.description: The arytenoid rotates and glides at the cricoarytenoid joint to move the vocal fold.

explanation: Marker A identifies the Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle. Lateral cricoarytenoid rotates the arytenoid to adduct the vocal fold.

distractorExplanations.A: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle is not the marked target. Posterior cricoarytenoid abducts the vocal folds by rotating the arytenoid cartilages.
distractorExplanations.B: Oblique arytenoid muscle is not the marked target. The oblique arytenoid muscles cross between the arytenoids and help narrow the laryngeal inlet.
distractorExplanations.C: Thyroarytenoid muscle is not the marked target. Thyroarytenoid shortens the vocal fold by drawing the arytenoid toward the thyroid cartilage.

learningObjective: Identify the Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Cricothyroid muscle
annotations.description: Cricothyroid tilts the thyroid relative to the cricoid and increases vocal fold tension.

annotations.label: Vocal ligament
annotations.description: The vocal ligament extends from the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid vocal process.

annotations.label: Thyroid cartilage
annotations.description: The thyroid cartilage provides the anterior attachment for the vocal ligament and intrinsic muscles.

annotations.label: Cricoid cartilage
annotations.description: The cricoid supports the arytenoids and gives origin to the cricoarytenoid muscles.

annotations.label: Arytenoid cartilage
annotations.description: The arytenoid rotates and glides at the cricoarytenoid joint to move the vocal fold.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Vocal ligament. The vocal ligament extends from the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid vocal process.

distractorExplanations.B: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle is not the marked target. Posterior cricoarytenoid abducts the vocal folds by rotating the arytenoid cartilages.
distractorExplanations.C: Oblique arytenoid muscle is not the marked target. The oblique arytenoid muscles cross between the arytenoids and help narrow the laryngeal inlet.
distractorExplanations.D: Transverse arytenoid muscle is not the marked target. The transverse interarytenoid muscle draws the arytenoid cartilages together.

learningObjective: Identify the Vocal ligament and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Cervical parietal pleura. The cervical pleura extends above the first rib at the thoracic inlet.

distractorExplanations.B: Pulmonary ligament is not the marked target. The pulmonary ligament is a double layer of pleura extending below the lung root.
distractorExplanations.C: Costal parietal pleura is not the marked target. The costal pleura lines the inner surface of the thoracic wall.
distractorExplanations.D: Visceral pleura covering lung root is not the marked target. Visceral pleura covers the lung root and reflects into mediastinal pleura.

learningObjective: Identify the Cervical parietal pleura and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Epiglottis
annotations.description: The epiglottis projects above and behind the hyoid bone.

annotations.label: Hyoid bone
annotations.description: The hyoid lies superior to the thyroid cartilage and suspends the larynx.

annotations.label: Superior horn of thyroid cartilage
annotations.description: The superior horn extends upward from the posterior border of the thyroid lamina.

annotations.label: Thyrohyoid membrane
annotations.description: The thyrohyoid membrane spans between the hyoid and thyroid cartilage.

annotations.label: Thyroid cartilage lamina
annotations.description: A thyroid lamina is one of the two broad plates forming the thyroid cartilage.

annotations.label: Median cricothyroid ligament
annotations.description: This thickened midline ligament connects the thyroid cartilage to the cricoid arch.

annotations.label: Superior thyroid notch
annotations.description: The superior thyroid notch lies in the upper border of the thyroid cartilage at the midline.

annotations.label: Inferior horn of thyroid cartilage
annotations.description: The inferior horn extends downward to articulate with the cricoid cartilage.

annotations.label: Cricoid cartilage
annotations.description: The cricoid cartilage forms the complete ring below the thyroid cartilage.

annotations.label: Trachea
annotations.description: The trachea continues inferiorly from the larynx below the cricoid cartilage.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Inferior horn of thyroid cartilage. The inferior horn extends downward to articulate with the cricoid cartilage.

distractorExplanations.A: Superior horn of thyroid cartilage is not the marked target. The superior horn extends upward from the posterior border of the thyroid lamina.
distractorExplanations.C: Thyrohyoid membrane is not the marked target. The thyrohyoid membrane spans between the hyoid and thyroid cartilage.
distractorExplanations.D: Epiglottis is not the marked target. The epiglottis projects above and behind the hyoid bone.

learningObjective: Identify the Inferior horn of thyroid cartilage and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Superior laryngeal nerve. The superior laryngeal nerve divides into internal and external branches.

distractorExplanations.B: External laryngeal nerve is not the marked target. The external branch descends to supply cricothyroid.
distractorExplanations.C: Internal laryngeal nerve is not the marked target. The internal branch passes through the thyrohyoid membrane to provide laryngeal sensation above the vocal folds.
distractorExplanations.D: Cricothyroid muscle is not the marked target. Cricothyroid receives its motor supply from the external laryngeal nerve.

learningObjective: Identify the Superior laryngeal nerve and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Superior laryngeal nerve
annotations.description: The superior laryngeal nerve divides into internal and external branches.

annotations.label: Internal laryngeal nerve
annotations.description: The internal branch passes through the thyrohyoid membrane to provide laryngeal sensation above the vocal folds.

annotations.label: External laryngeal nerve
annotations.description: The external branch descends to supply cricothyroid.

annotations.label: Cricothyroid muscle
annotations.description: Cricothyroid receives its motor supply from the external laryngeal nerve.

annotations.label: Recurrent laryngeal nerve
annotations.description: The recurrent laryngeal nerve ascends toward the larynx and supplies most intrinsic muscles.

annotations.label: Galen anastomosis
annotations.description: The ansa of Galen is a communication between internal and recurrent laryngeal nerve branches.

annotations.label: Thyroarytenoid muscle
annotations.description: Thyroarytenoid extends between thyroid and arytenoid cartilages.

annotations.label: Vocalis muscle
annotations.description: Vocalis is the medial part of thyroarytenoid alongside the vocal ligament.

annotations.label: Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle
annotations.description: Lateral cricoarytenoid adducts the vocal fold by rotating the arytenoid.

annotations.label: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle
annotations.description: Posterior cricoarytenoid is the intrinsic muscle that abducts the vocal fold.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Recurrent laryngeal nerve. The recurrent laryngeal nerve ascends toward the larynx and supplies most intrinsic muscles.

distractorExplanations.B: Internal laryngeal nerve is not the marked target. The internal branch passes through the thyrohyoid membrane to provide laryngeal sensation above the vocal folds.
distractorExplanations.C: Superior laryngeal nerve is not the marked target. The superior laryngeal nerve divides into internal and external branches.
distractorExplanations.D: External laryngeal nerve is not the marked target. The external branch descends to supply cricothyroid.

learningObjective: Identify the Recurrent laryngeal nerve and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Visceral layer of serous pericardium. The visceral serous pericardium covers the heart surface and is also called the epicardium.

distractorExplanations.B: Fibrous pericardium is not the marked target. The fibrous pericardium forms the tough outer pericardial sac, continuous superiorly with the adventitia of the great vessels.
distractorExplanations.C: Parietal layer of serous pericardium is not the marked target. The parietal serous layer lines the inner surface of the fibrous pericardium and faces the pericardial cavity.
distractorExplanations.D: Pericardial cavity is not the marked target. The pericardial cavity is the potential space between the parietal and visceral serous pericardial layers.

learningObjective: Identify the Visceral layer of serous pericardium and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Superior vena cava. The superior vena cava descends on the right side of the superior mediastinum and opens into the superior aspect of the right atrium.

distractorExplanations.A: Ascending aorta is not the marked target. The ascending aorta rises from the left ventricle and continues into the aortic arch. The coronary arteries arise near its root.
distractorExplanations.B: Transverse pericardial sinus is not the marked target. The transverse pericardial sinus passes behind the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk and anterior to the venous structures.
distractorExplanations.C: Right pulmonary artery is not the marked target. The right pulmonary artery passes toward the right lung behind the ascending aorta and superior vena cava.

learningObjective: Identify the Superior vena cava and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Superior vena cava
annotations.description: The superior vena cava descends on the right side of the superior mediastinum and opens into the superior aspect of the right atrium.

annotations.label: Ascending aorta
annotations.description: The ascending aorta rises from the left ventricle and continues into the aortic arch. The coronary arteries arise near its root.

annotations.label: Transverse pericardial sinus
annotations.description: The transverse pericardial sinus passes behind the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk and anterior to the venous structures.

annotations.label: Right pulmonary artery
annotations.description: The right pulmonary artery passes toward the right lung behind the ascending aorta and superior vena cava.

annotations.label: Right pulmonary veins
annotations.description: The right pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the right lung and enter the right side of the left atrium.

annotations.label: Inferior vena cava
annotations.description: The inferior vena cava passes through the diaphragm and enters the inferior aspect of the right atrium.

annotations.label: Arch of aorta
annotations.description: The aortic arch curves superiorly and posteriorly over the root of the left lung and gives rise to the great arteries supplying the head, neck and upper limbs.

annotations.label: Left pulmonary artery
annotations.description: The left pulmonary artery branches from the pulmonary trunk and travels toward the root of the left lung beneath the aortic arch.

annotations.label: Left pulmonary veins
annotations.description: The left pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the left lung to the left atrium.

annotations.label: Oblique pericardial sinus
annotations.description: The oblique pericardial sinus is the blind recess behind the left atrium bounded by pericardial reflections around the pulmonary veins and inferior vena cava.

annotations.label: Fibrous pericardium
annotations.description: The fibrous pericardium forms the tough outer pericardial sac, continuous superiorly with the adventitia of the great vessels.

annotations.label: Descending thoracic aorta
annotations.description: The descending thoracic aorta runs through the posterior mediastinum to the left of the vertebral column before passing through the diaphragm.

explanation: Marker A identifies the Descending thoracic aorta. The descending thoracic aorta runs through the posterior mediastinum to the left of the vertebral column before passing through the diaphragm.

distractorExplanations.A: Superior vena cava is not the marked target. The superior vena cava descends on the right side of the superior mediastinum and opens into the superior aspect of the right atrium.
distractorExplanations.B: Right pulmonary artery is not the marked target. The right pulmonary artery passes toward the right lung behind the ascending aorta and superior vena cava.
distractorExplanations.D: Transverse pericardial sinus is not the marked target. The transverse pericardial sinus passes behind the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk and anterior to the venous structures.

learningObjective: Identify the Descending thoracic aorta and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Superior vena cava
annotations.description: The superior vena cava descends on the right side of the superior mediastinum and opens into the superior aspect of the right atrium.

annotations.label: Ascending aorta
annotations.description: The ascending aorta rises from the left ventricle and continues into the aortic arch. The coronary arteries arise near its root.

annotations.label: Transverse pericardial sinus
annotations.description: The transverse pericardial sinus passes behind the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk and anterior to the venous structures.

annotations.label: Right pulmonary artery
annotations.description: The right pulmonary artery passes toward the right lung behind the ascending aorta and superior vena cava.

annotations.label: Right pulmonary veins
annotations.description: The right pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the right lung and enter the right side of the left atrium.

annotations.label: Inferior vena cava
annotations.description: The inferior vena cava passes through the diaphragm and enters the inferior aspect of the right atrium.

annotations.label: Arch of aorta
annotations.description: The aortic arch curves superiorly and posteriorly over the root of the left lung and gives rise to the great arteries supplying the head, neck and upper limbs.

annotations.label: Left pulmonary artery
annotations.description: The left pulmonary artery branches from the pulmonary trunk and travels toward the root of the left lung beneath the aortic arch.

annotations.label: Left pulmonary veins
annotations.description: The left pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the left lung to the left atrium.

annotations.label: Oblique pericardial sinus
annotations.description: The oblique pericardial sinus is the blind recess behind the left atrium bounded by pericardial reflections around the pulmonary veins and inferior vena cava.

annotations.label: Fibrous pericardium
annotations.description: The fibrous pericardium forms the tough outer pericardial sac, continuous superiorly with the adventitia of the great vessels.

annotations.label: Descending thoracic aorta
annotations.description: The descending thoracic aorta runs through the posterior mediastinum to the left of the vertebral column before passing through the diaphragm.

annotations.label: Superior vena cava
annotations.description: The superior vena cava descends on the right side of the superior mediastinum and opens into the superior aspect of the right atrium.

annotations.label: Arch of aorta
annotations.description: The aortic arch curves superiorly and posteriorly over the root of the left lung and gives rise to the great arteries supplying the head, neck and upper limbs.

annotations.label: Right auricle
annotations.description: The right auricle is the muscular appendage of the right atrium that overlaps the root of the ascending aorta.

annotations.label: Right atrium
annotations.description: The right atrium receives the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava and coronary sinus and opens into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.

annotations.label: Pulmonary trunk
annotations.description: The pulmonary trunk leaves the right ventricle and divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries.

annotations.label: Left auricle
annotations.description: The left auricle is the muscular appendage of the left atrium that projects beside the pulmonary trunk.

annotations.label: Pulmonary valve
annotations.description: The pulmonary valve guards the outflow of the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk and has three semilunar leaflets.

annotations.label: Conus arteriosus
annotations.description: The conus arteriosus is the smooth outflow region of the right ventricle leading to the pulmonary valve.

annotations.label: Septal papillary muscle
annotations.description: The septal papillary muscle belongs to the right ventricular tricuspid apparatus and attaches chordae to valve leaflets.

annotations.label: Septomarginal trabecula
annotations.description: The septomarginal trabecula, or moderator band, crosses the right ventricular cavity from the septum toward the anterior papillary muscle.

annotations.label: Tricuspid valve
annotations.description: The tricuspid valve guards the right atrioventricular opening. Its leaflets connect by chordae tendineae to right ventricular papillary muscles.

annotations.label: Chordae tendineae
annotations.description: These tendinous cords connect atrioventricular valve leaflets to papillary muscles and help prevent leaflet prolapse during ventricular contraction.

annotations.label: Anterior papillary muscle
annotations.description: The anterior papillary muscle shown here belongs to the right ventricle and anchors tricuspid valve leaflets through chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Posterior papillary muscle
annotations.description: The posterior papillary muscle shown here belongs to the right ventricle and anchors tricuspid valve leaflets through chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Trabeculae carneae
annotations.description: Trabeculae carneae are the irregular muscular ridges of the ventricular wall, contrasting with the smoother ventricular outflow tracts.

annotations.label: Arch of aorta
annotations.description: The aortic arch curves superiorly and posteriorly over the root of the left lung and gives rise to the great arteries supplying the head, neck and upper limbs.

annotations.label: Anterior cusp of mitral valve
annotations.description: The anterior, or aortic, leaflet of the mitral valve lies adjacent to the aortic outlet and attaches to chordae tendineae from the ventricular papillary muscles.

annotations.label: Chordae tendineae
annotations.description: These tendinous cords connect atrioventricular valve leaflets to papillary muscles and help prevent leaflet prolapse during ventricular contraction.

annotations.label: Anterior papillary muscle
annotations.description: The anterior papillary muscle shown here belongs to the left ventricle and anchors mitral valve leaflets through chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Trabeculae carneae
annotations.description: Trabeculae carneae are the irregular muscular ridges of the ventricular wall, contrasting with the smoother ventricular outflow tracts.

annotations.label: Posterior papillary muscle

annotations.label: Posterior cusp of mitral valve

annotations.label: Left atrium

annotations.label: Pulmonary veins

subject: anatomy
topic: Surface features of a typical rib
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Head of rib. The head forms the posterior vertebral end of a rib. A typical head bears two facets for articulation with adjacent vertebral bodies.

distractorExplanations.A: Angle of rib is not the marked target. The angle is the point of greatest curvature of the rib, lateral to its tubercle.
distractorExplanations.C: Tubercle of rib is not the marked target. The rib tubercle lies at the junction of the neck and shaft and includes articular and non-articular parts.
distractorExplanations.D: Neck of rib is not the marked target. The neck is the short segment between the rib head and tubercle.

learningObjective: Identify the Head of rib and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

media.alt: Surface features of a typical rib. Internal aspect with detail of posterior end. Original source diagram with leader lines.
media.caption: Surface features of a typical rib

annotations.label: Head of rib
annotations.description: The head forms the posterior vertebral end of a rib. A typical head bears two facets for articulation with adjacent vertebral bodies.

annotations.label: Tubercle of rib
annotations.description: The rib tubercle lies at the junction of the neck and shaft and includes articular and non-articular parts.

annotations.label: Angle of rib
annotations.description: The angle is the point of greatest curvature of the rib, lateral to its tubercle.

annotations.label: Neck of rib
annotations.description: The neck is the short segment between the rib head and tubercle.

annotations.label: Internal surface of rib
annotations.description: The internal surface is the concave surface facing the thoracic cavity and includes the costal groove near its inferior border.

annotations.label: Costal groove
annotations.description: The costal groove runs along the internal surface near the inferior border of a rib and shelters the main intercostal neurovascular bundle.

annotations.label: Costal cartilage
annotations.description: Costal cartilage continues the anterior end of a rib and contributes to the flexible anterior thoracic wall.

annotations.label: External surface of rib
annotations.description: The external surface is the convex surface of the rib facing away from the thoracic cavity.

annotations.label: Crest of head of rib
annotations.description: The crest separates the two articular facets on the head of a typical rib and provides attachment for the intra-articular ligament.

annotations.label: Articular facets of head of rib
annotations.description: A typical rib head has two articular facets separated by a crest. These facets articulate with the bodies of adjacent thoracic vertebrae.

annotations.label: Articular facet of tubercle
annotations.description: The smooth articular part of the rib tubercle meets the transverse costal facet of the corresponding thoracic vertebra.

annotations.label: Non-articular part of tubercle
annotations.description: The rough non-articular part of the rib tubercle provides attachment for the lateral costotransverse ligament.

distractorExplanations.B: Head of rib is not the marked target. The head forms the posterior vertebral end of a rib. A typical head bears two facets for articulation with adjacent vertebral bodies.
distractorExplanations.C: Angle of rib is not the marked target. The angle is the point of greatest curvature of the rib, lateral to its tubercle.
distractorExplanations.D: Tubercle of rib is not the marked target. The rib tubercle lies at the junction of the neck and shaft and includes articular and non-articular parts.

learningObjective: Identify the Internal surface of rib and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Pectoralis major. Pectoralis major is the broad superficial muscle of the anterior chest. Its removal in this figure reveals deeper pectoral structures.

distractorExplanations.A: Pectoralis minor is not the marked target. Pectoralis minor lies deep to pectoralis major and passes from the upper ribs to the coracoid process.
distractorExplanations.C: Subclavius is not the marked target. Subclavius is the small muscle immediately beneath the clavicle, enclosed by the clavipectoral fascia.
distractorExplanations.D: Clavipectoral fascia is not the marked target. The clavipectoral fascia lies deep to pectoralis major and encloses subclavius and pectoralis minor.

learningObjective: Identify the Pectoralis major and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
topic: Left vagus and aortic arch relations
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Oesophagus. The oesophagus lies posterior to the trachea and continues through the posterior mediastinum toward the diaphragm.

distractorExplanations.A: Pulmonary trunk is not the marked target. The pulmonary trunk leaves the right ventricle and divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries.
distractorExplanations.C: Right main bronchus is not the marked target. The right main bronchus passes from the tracheal bifurcation toward the root of the right lung.
distractorExplanations.D: Trachea is not the marked target. The trachea descends in front of the oesophagus and divides into the right and left main bronchi.

learningObjective: Identify the Oesophagus and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.description: The pulmonary trunk leaves the right ventricle and divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries.

annotations.label: Left recurrent laryngeal nerve
annotations.description: The left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops beneath the aortic arch beside the ligamentum arteriosum and ascends toward the larynx.

annotations.label: Left subclavian artery
annotations.description: The left subclavian artery is the third usual branch of the aortic arch and travels toward the root of the neck and upper limb.

annotations.label: Left vagus nerve

annotations.label: Arch of aorta

annotations.description: The left pulmonary artery branches from the pulmonary trunk and travels toward the root of the left lung beneath the aortic arch.

annotations.label: Left main bronchus
annotations.description: The left main bronchus passes below the aortic arch toward the root of the left lung.

annotations.label: Descending thoracic aorta
annotations.description: The descending thoracic aorta runs through the posterior mediastinum to the left of the vertebral column before passing through the diaphragm.
