annotations.description: The oesophagus lies posterior to the trachea and continues through the posterior mediastinum toward the diaphragm.

annotations.label: Trachea
annotations.description: The trachea descends in front of the oesophagus and divides into the right and left main bronchi.

annotations.label: Right main bronchus
annotations.description: The right main bronchus passes from the tracheal bifurcation toward the root of the right lung.

annotations.label: Pulmonary trunk
annotations.description: The pulmonary trunk leaves the right ventricle and divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries.

annotations.label: Left recurrent laryngeal nerve
annotations.description: The left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops beneath the aortic arch beside the ligamentum arteriosum and ascends toward the larynx.

annotations.label: Left subclavian artery
annotations.description: The left subclavian artery is the third usual branch of the aortic arch and travels toward the root of the neck and upper limb.

annotations.label: Left vagus nerve
annotations.description: The left vagus nerve crosses the aortic arch, gives off the left recurrent laryngeal nerve, and continues posterior to the root of the left lung.

annotations.label: Arch of aorta
annotations.description: The aortic arch curves superiorly and posteriorly over the root of the left lung and gives rise to the great arteries supplying the head, neck and upper limbs.

annotations.label: Ligamentum arteriosum
annotations.description: The ligamentum arteriosum connects the left pulmonary artery to the underside of the aortic arch and is the remnant of the ductus arteriosus.

annotations.label: Left pulmonary artery
annotations.description: The left pulmonary artery branches from the pulmonary trunk and travels toward the root of the left lung beneath the aortic arch.

annotations.label: Left main bronchus
annotations.description: The left main bronchus passes below the aortic arch toward the root of the left lung.

annotations.label: Descending thoracic aorta
annotations.description: The descending thoracic aorta runs through the posterior mediastinum to the left of the vertebral column before passing through the diaphragm.

subject: anatomy

topic: Great vessels and recurrent laryngeal nerves
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Right recurrent laryngeal nerve. The right recurrent laryngeal nerve branches from the right vagus, loops beneath the right subclavian artery and ascends toward the larynx.

distractorExplanations.B: Right common carotid artery is not the marked target. The right common carotid artery arises from the brachiocephalic trunk and ascends into the neck.
distractorExplanations.C: Right subclavian artery is not the marked target. The right subclavian artery arises from the brachiocephalic trunk and passes toward the root of the neck and upper limb.
distractorExplanations.D: Brachiocephalic trunk is not the marked target. The brachiocephalic trunk is the first major branch of the aortic arch. It divides into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.

learningObjective: Identify the Right recurrent laryngeal nerve and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
topic: Thoracic sympathetic trunks and splanchnic nerves
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Sympathetic trunk. The thoracic sympathetic trunk runs vertically beside the vertebral column and gives rise to the thoracic splanchnic nerves.

distractorExplanations.A: Thoracic spinal nerve is not the marked target. A thoracic spinal nerve emerges near the intervertebral foramen and communicates with the sympathetic trunk through rami communicantes.
distractorExplanations.C: Lesser splanchnic nerve is not the marked target. The lesser thoracic splanchnic nerve descends from the lower thoracic sympathetic trunk, below the greater splanchnic nerve, toward abdominal autonomic plexuses.
distractorExplanations.D: Greater splanchnic nerve is not the marked target. The greater thoracic splanchnic nerve descends medially from the thoracic sympathetic trunk toward the diaphragm and abdominal prevertebral plexuses.

learningObjective: Identify the Sympathetic trunk and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Manubrium of sternum. The manubrium forms the superior part of the sternum and bears the clavicular notches and the first costal notches.

distractorExplanations.B: Sternal angle and manubriosternal joint is not the marked target. The manubriosternal joint forms the sternal angle between the manubrium and body of the sternum.
distractorExplanations.C: Body of sternum is not the marked target. The body forms the elongated middle part of the sternum between the manubrium and xiphoid process.
distractorExplanations.D: Xiphoid process is not the marked target. The xiphoid process forms the small inferior end of the sternum below the sternal body.

learningObjective: Identify the Manubrium of sternum and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the External intercostal muscle. The external intercostal is the outer muscular layer of the intercostal space. Its fibers descend forward between adjacent ribs.

distractorExplanations.A: Endothoracic fascia is not the marked target. The endothoracic fascia lines the inner surface of the thoracic wall between the innermost musculoskeletal layer and the parietal pleura.
distractorExplanations.C: Innermost intercostal muscle is not the marked target. The innermost intercostal forms the deepest intercostal muscular layer. The main neurovascular bundle lies between it and the internal intercostal muscle.
distractorExplanations.D: Internal intercostal muscle is not the marked target. The internal intercostal lies deep to the external intercostal. The neurovascular plane separates it from the innermost layer.

learningObjective: Identify the External intercostal muscle and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Azygos vein. The azygos vein ascends on the right side of the vertebral column and arches over the root of the right lung to enter the superior vena cava.

distractorExplanations.A: Hemiazygos vein is not the marked target. The hemiazygos vein ascends on the lower left side of the vertebral column and crosses to join the azygos vein.
distractorExplanations.C: Descending thoracic aorta is not the marked target. The descending thoracic aorta runs through the posterior mediastinum to the left of the vertebral column before passing through the diaphragm.
distractorExplanations.D: Accessory hemiazygos vein is not the marked target. This vein drains the upper left posterior intercostal spaces and crosses the vertebral column to join the azygos vein.

learningObjective: Identify the Azygos vein and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.label: Superior mediastinum
annotations.description: The superior mediastinum lies above the transverse thoracic plane and contains the aortic arch, major veins, trachea and oesophagus.

annotations.label: Thymus
annotations.description: The thymus lies behind the sternum, occupying the anterior part of the superior mediastinum and extending variably into the anterior mediastinum.

annotations.label: Manubrium
annotations.description: The manubrium forms the superior part of the sternum and joins the sternal body at the sternal angle.

annotations.label: Sternal angle
annotations.description: The sternal angle marks the junction of the manubrium and body and is an anterior landmark for the transverse thoracic plane.

annotations.label: Anterior mediastinum
annotations.description: The anterior mediastinum lies between the sternum and the pericardium below the transverse thoracic plane.

annotations.label: Middle mediastinum
annotations.description: The middle mediastinum contains the heart and pericardium together with the roots of the great vessels.

annotations.label: Diaphragm
annotations.description: The diaphragm forms the muscular partition between thorax and abdomen and closes the inferior thoracic aperture.

annotations.label: Inferior vena cava
annotations.description: The inferior vena cava passes through the diaphragm and enters the inferior aspect of the right atrium.

annotations.label: Posterior mediastinum
annotations.description: The posterior mediastinum lies behind the pericardium and contains the oesophagus, descending thoracic aorta, azygos system and thoracic duct.

annotations.label: Trachea
annotations.description: The trachea descends in front of the oesophagus and divides into the right and left main bronchi.

annotations.label: Left subclavian artery
annotations.description: The left subclavian artery is the third usual branch of the aortic arch and travels toward the root of the neck and upper limb.

annotations.label: Arch of aorta
annotations.description: The aortic arch curves superiorly and posteriorly over the root of the left lung and gives rise to the great arteries supplying the head, neck and upper limbs.

annotations.label: Right pulmonary artery
annotations.description: The right pulmonary artery passes toward the right lung behind the ascending aorta and superior vena cava.

annotations.label: Left main bronchus
annotations.description: The left main bronchus passes below the aortic arch toward the root of the left lung.

annotations.label: Descending thoracic aorta
annotations.description: The descending thoracic aorta runs through the posterior mediastinum to the left of the vertebral column before passing through the diaphragm.

annotations.label: Oesophagus
annotations.description: The oesophagus lies posterior to the trachea and continues through the posterior mediastinum toward the diaphragm.

explanation: Marker A identifies the Left atrium. The left atrium receives the pulmonary veins and forms most of the posterior base of the heart.

distractorExplanations.A: Coronary sinus is not the marked target. The coronary sinus occupies the posterior atrioventricular groove and receives major cardiac veins before opening into the right atrium.
distractorExplanations.C: Circumflex artery is not the marked target. The circumflex branch of the left coronary artery follows the left part of the atrioventricular groove toward the posterior surface of the heart.
distractorExplanations.D: Great cardiac vein is not the marked target. The great cardiac vein ascends in the anterior interventricular groove and then follows the left atrioventricular groove toward the coronary sinus.

learningObjective: Identify the Left atrium and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

explanation: Marker A identifies the Left atrium. The left atrium receives the pulmonary veins and forms most of the posterior base of the heart.

distractorExplanations.A: Apex of heart is not the marked target. The left ventricle forms the apex of the heart, which points inferiorly, anteriorly and to the left.
distractorExplanations.B: Coronary sinus is not the marked target. The coronary sinus occupies the posterior atrioventricular groove and receives major cardiac veins before opening into the right atrium.
distractorExplanations.C: Great cardiac vein is not the marked target. The great cardiac vein ascends in the anterior interventricular groove and then follows the left atrioventricular groove toward the coronary sinus.

learningObjective: Identify the Left atrium and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

subject: anatomy
topic: Valves and vessels at the ventricular base
prompt: Which structure is indicated by callout A?
explanation: Marker A identifies the Pulmonary valve. The pulmonary valve guards the outflow of the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk and has three semilunar leaflets.

distractorExplanations.A: Left coronary artery is not the marked target. The left coronary artery arises from the left aortic sinus and passes between the pulmonary trunk and left auricle before dividing into its principal branches.
distractorExplanations.C: Right coronary artery is not the marked target. The right coronary artery arises from the right aortic sinus and follows the right atrioventricular groove.
distractorExplanations.D: Aortic valve is not the marked target. The aortic valve guards the outlet from the left ventricle into the aorta and consists of three semilunar leaflets.

learningObjective: Identify the Pulmonary valve and distinguish it from adjacent structures.

annotations.description: The left coronary artery arises from the left aortic sinus and passes between the pulmonary trunk and left auricle before dividing into its principal branches.

annotations.label: Right coronary artery
annotations.description: The right coronary artery arises from the right aortic sinus and follows the right atrioventricular groove.

annotations.label: Atrioventricular bundle
annotations.description: The atrioventricular bundle traverses the fibrous cardiac skeleton and continues into the ventricular conduction system.

annotations.label: Coronary sinus
annotations.description: The coronary sinus occupies the posterior atrioventricular groove and receives major cardiac veins before opening into the right atrium.

annotations.label: Middle cardiac vein
annotations.description: The middle cardiac vein follows the inferior interventricular groove and drains into the coronary sinus near its right atrial opening.

annotations.label: Inferior interventricular artery
annotations.description: This artery descends in the inferior, traditionally posterior, interventricular groove. The illustrated arrangement shows it arising from the right coronary artery.
